builds.name: Reference: Ranked bot core
builds.goal: Reference for Ashe: the core and runes ranked Emerald+ bot players use most (16,718 ranked Emerald+ games with this core on OP.GG, patch 16.20, 57% win rate).
builds.hypothesis: A ranged attacker who maintains slows to kite and uses scouting and a long-range stun to start favorable fights. The current adc provider core anchors this plan; later slots are observed options or reviewed kit completions. Core in purchase order: Hexoptics C44 → Phantom Dancer → Infinity Edge. Lethal Tempo keystone as played in those games. Remaining slots: Berserker's Greaves, Lord Dominik's Regards, Guardian Angel.
builds.summary: The proven bot baseline: Hexoptics C44 → Phantom Dancer → Infinity Edge, with Lethal Tempo.
testPlan: Play it in bot as your control build. Follow the purchase order; the core (Hexoptics C44 → Phantom Dancer → Infinity Edge) is what ranked players complete first.
Record kills, deaths, damage dealt and the minute you finish each core item, then compare other builds against these numbers in similar games.
Adapt the last two items to the enemy team: armor or magic resist against fed carries, anti-heal against healing, penetration once enemies stack resists.
failureConditions: Your results with this build fall clearly below the 57% ranked baseline over several games in the same role.
The enemy team composition makes the core items poor answers; swap the flexible slots before abandoning the core.
tradeoffs: Proven and predictable, so opponents know what to expect. It is a starting point, not the best build for every matchup.
The observed core and individual options do not establish six-item build statistics. Late slots are kit-based inferences.
Six-slot completion is our kit-based inference, not an observed six-item win-rate build.  Situational options replace an appropriate slot; they are not added as a seventh item.
buyOrder: Core in purchase order: Hexoptics C44 → Phantom Dancer → Infinity Edge.
Boots after the first item unless the lane needs them earlier.
coverageNotes: Source: OP.GG ranked Emerald+ solo/duo, patch 16.20, checked 2026-10-14. Core items and rune page are observed; later slots are observed options or reviewed completions. Win rates describe those games, not a prediction for yours.

kitEvidence.formula:
Passive: Ashe's Attacks grant a stack for [4] seconds. At [4] stacks, she may activate this Ability.

Active: Ashe gains [20 / 30 / 40 / 50 / 60]% Attack Speed and her Attacks deal [(1.1 / 1.15 / 1.2 / 1.25 / 1.3) × AD] damage instead for [6] seconds.

Ashe launches a crystal arrow of ice that Stuns the first champion hit and deals [200 / 400 / 600 + (1.2) × AP] magic damage. The Stun duration increases with distance travelled, up to [3.5] seconds. Surrounding enemies are Slowed by Frost Shot.

Ashe fires a volley of [7 / 8 / 9 / 10 / 11] arrows, each dealing [60 / 95 / 130 / 165 / 200 + (1) × AD[statFormula=2]] physical damage. Enemies can be hit by multiple arrows, but only take damage from the first.

Ashe sends forth a hawk to grant vision for 5 seconds anywhere on the map. It also reveals the area around it as it flies.

This Ability has 2 charges ([(runtimeCooldownMultiplier) × (90 / 80 / 70 / 60 / 50)] second recharge).

Ashe's Attacks and Abilities Slow by [characterLevelInterpolation(0.2 → 0.3; raw flags preserved)] for [2] seconds. Attacks deal [1 + ((1 + (1) × Stat(9)[statFormula=2])) × Stat(8)] damage.

Ashe's critical strikes deal no extra damage, instead increasing the Slow to [characterLevelInterpolation(0.4 → 0.6; raw flags preserved)] decaying.

builds.name: Arrow-first hybrid barrage
builds.summary: Follow an AP arrow catch with three rapid attacks.
builds.goal: Follow an AP arrow catch with three rapid attacks.
builds.hypothesis: Enchanted Crystal Arrow carries a 1.2 AP magic ratio and up to 3.5 seconds of stun. Fiendhunter Bolts grants three accelerated crit attacks after R, Nashor supports these actual attacks, and Malignance rewards R's magic hit. This tests pick burst plus follow-up, while Q still needs four attack stacks before activation.
testPlan: Required state: Need a clear arrow lane and ability to reach attack range during the stun.
Measure arrow alone, three attacks and then Q availability at several arrow distances.

Run three trials at matched level, ranks, gold and target defenses. Repeat against a moving opponent with a fixed incoming damage pattern. Record damage packets, missed actions, resource cost and survival separately.
Keep souls, health/mana, form, item/rune stacks, transformations and game time finite and explicitly recorded. No free full ramp or infinite scaling.
failureConditions: A global arrow may land beyond follow-up range; low AD weakens extended Q trades.
The narrow damage gain does not repay lost access, survival, wave control or allied utility.
tradeoffs: Rejected assumption: Ashe crits enhance Frost Shot behavior; do not assume normal bonus crit damage on her attacks.
Confidence: speculative. Source-compatible reasoning is not in-game validation or proof of novelty/optimality.
buyOrder: Candidate six slots: Fiendhunter Bolts, Malignance, Nashor's Tooth, Rabadon's Deathcap, Cryptbloom, Berserker's Greaves. Compare two-item checkpoints before the final six-slot test; this list is not a lane shopping order.
Keep role-appropriate starters, boots and support quest/vision obligations. If the full candidate assumes farmed income, compare it separately from support income.
coverageNotes: Only Cassiopeia Q/E and Sett W have numerical adapters. Even there, these other objectives and item/rune interactions may fall outside the model.
Proc inheritance, crit, pet hits and conditional helpers remain uncertain until observed. No completed mathematical maximum is claimed.

builds.name: Situational adaptation: Critical duel
builds.goal: Situational adaptation for Ashe: adapt to the specified fight rather than assume one universal build
builds.hypothesis: A ranged attacker who maintains slows to kite and uses scouting and a long-range stun to start favorable fights. Can constant attack slows and scouting/R initiation generate more teamfight uptime, or does an active-support route sacrifice too much personal damage? Use a fixed Q readiness state. Crit attacks and a conditional shield test repeated duel windows.
builds.summary: Crit attacks and a conditional shield test repeated duel windows.
testPlan: Kit question for Ashe: Can constant attack slows and scouting/R initiation generate more teamfight uptime, or does an active-support route sacrifice too much personal damage? Use a fixed Q readiness state.

Start with the early core (Kraken, then Navori if attack-driven recycling works) plus appropriate boots at matched gold. Record level, actual ability ranks, forms, resource and item transformations; six-item results do not establish lane strength. Use your intended lane or jungle role; jungle starters and early consumables are outside the final six slots.

Compare against the reference route at the same level, gold spent, finite stacks and opponent setup. Record unused gold; isolate an item change before changing runes. Run three repeatable trials of a short trade and a ten-second fight. Record damage actually landed, attacks/casts, misses, remaining resource and survival. Record available/max mana and any transformed mana-item state.

Measure the actual interaction before granting item/rune procs: Crit attacks and a conditional shield test repeated duel windows. Test once stationary, then with a moving opponent and a fixed incoming damage pattern. Choose the opponent profile this defensive route is intended to address, then repeat against the wrong damage type.

Q evidence: Ashe builds up Focus by attacking. At maximum Focus, Ashe can cast Ranger's Focus to consume all stacks of Focus, temporarily increasing her Attack Speed and transforming her basic attack into a powerful flurry attack for the duration. Keep finite champion/item/rune stacks explicit. Use Practice Tool, a custom match or your own replay; no numerical adapter is available for this champion.
failureConditions: A Lifeline slot excludes Sterak/Maw; melee access or ranged spacing must be earned.

The route fails Ashe's stated kit question: Can constant attack slows and scouting/R initiation generate more teamfight uptime, or does an active-support route sacrifice too much personal damage? Use a fixed Q readiness state.
Higher dummy damage is offset by fewer landed actions, deaths before the useful window, or worse ally utility.
tradeoffs: A Lifeline slot excludes Sterak/Maw; melee access or ranged spacing must be earned.
Full cost 16,550 gold; delayed items, resource starvation and the two-item spike must be judged separately.
Counter-items are conditional. Change boots/defense for the real matchup, then record the modified setup.
buyOrder: Kraken, then Navori if attack-driven recycling works. Adapt component timing to lane/jungle pressure; do not blindly follow the displayed six-item order.
Keep appropriate boots while building the early core; swap boots only when the measured matchup justifies it.
Infinity Edge, Immortal Shieldbow, Lord Dominik's Regards are later or conditional slots; do not postpone necessary protection for a six-item ceiling.
Record available/max mana and any transformed mana-item state.
coverageNotes: No numerical damage or survival adapter exists for this champion. Loading this proposal opens a manual test sheet, not calculated damage.
Source formulas remain in Champion kit. Symbolic values, unresolved tokens and helper records are evidence to inspect, not a certified executable simulator.
Legal source item/rune references were checked; retained map flags cannot prove every live-shop condition. Confirm shop eligibility, exact on-hit/on-attack rules and real proc cooldowns in game.

builds.name: Volley pursuit bruiser
builds.summary: Use repeated physical Volley to expose and soften fleeing teams.
builds.goal: Use repeated physical Volley to expose and soften fleeing teams.
builds.hypothesis: Volley has an AD statFormula=2 expression and only its first arrow damages a given target. Muramana offers mana and physical spell payload subject to proc rules; Cleaver shreds armor through physical damage, Shojin supports repeated abilities, and Youmuu supplies physical penetration and an active movement burst for positioning. Hawkshot helps choose safe approach lines between casts.
testPlan: Required state: Need charged Manamune, real W hits and allies able to exploit softened targets.
Record W intervals and armor stacks over repeated volleys, versus a normal attack build.

Run three trials at matched level, ranks, gold and target defenses. Repeat against a moving opponent with a fixed incoming damage pattern. Record damage packets, missed actions, resource cost and survival separately.
Keep souls, health/mana, form, item/rune stacks, transformations and game time finite and explicitly recorded. No free full ramp or infinite scaling.
failureConditions: Low attack DPS and single-hit Volley cannot rapidly shred one target; R remains weak without AP.
The narrow damage gain does not repay lost access, survival, wave control or allied utility.
tradeoffs: Rejected assumption: Multiple arrows striking one champion do not grant multiple damage events or full Cleaver stacks.
Confidence: plausible. Source-compatible reasoning is not in-game validation or proof of novelty/optimality.
